library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Gibiansky_2019_obinutuzumab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Gibiansky_2019_obinutuzumab"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/bcp.13974> (open access; the parameter
  estimates of the final model are in Supplementary Table S5)

Obinutuzumab is a glycoengineered type II anti-CD20 IgG1 antibody. Gibiansky
2019 updated the population PK model of Gibiansky 2014 (packaged as
`Gibiansky_2014_obinutuzumab`) with the phase III GADOLIN study
(obinutuzumab plus bendamustine in rituximab-refractory indolent non-Hodgkin
lymphoma) and the phase II GATHER study (obinutuzumab plus CHOP in diffuse
large B-cell lymphoma), and used it to derive exposure for GADOLIN
exposure-response analyses. The structure is unchanged from 2014: two
compartments, and a total clearance made of a time-independent component
`CL_inf` and a time-dependent component `CL_T` that decays exponentially with
time since the first dose as CD20+ target cells are depleted:

`CL(t) = CL_T * exp(-k_des * t) + CL_inf`

The covariate model is new. Body weight, albumin, age, sex, disease type and
indolent lymphoma subtype, and baseline tumour size act on the clearances;
the partner chemotherapy (CHOP, bendamustine, or fludarabine +
cyclophosphamide) and marginal zone lymphoma act on the decay rate `k_des`.

# Population

The analysis pooled 16,301 serum concentrations from 961 patients in six
studies (Table S1): GAUSS (105), GAUGUIN (131), GAUDI (134), CLL11 (308),
GADOLIN (183) and GATHER (100). Disease types were CLL (342), indolent NHL
(469: follicular lymphoma 406, marginal zone lymphoma 35, small lymphocytic
lymphoma 22, Waldenstrom macroglobulinaemia 5), DLBCL (130) and mantle cell
lymphoma (20). Mean (SD) age was 64.1 (12.2) years, weight 77.4 (16.3) kg,
albumin 40.3 (5.18) g/L and baseline tumour size 4900 (5760) mm^2 (Table
S4). Intravenous doses ranged from 50 to 2000 mg. The sex distribution is not
reported.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Gibiansky_2019_obinutuzumab")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. The
table below collects them. The paper prints the parameter values (Table S5)
and the effect sizes at reference and illustrative covariate values (Table 1)
but no model code; the functional forms below are the ones that reproduce
every row of Table 1 (checked in the next section).

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl_exp_kdes` (k_des) | log(0.11 1/day) | Table S5; half-life 6.3 days (Results) |
| `lcl_exp_component` (CL_T) | log(0.154 L/day) | Table S5 |
| `lcl_exp_inf` (CL_inf) | log(0.0742 L/day) | Table S5; "74 mL/day" (Results) |
| `lvc` (V1) | log(2.72 L) | Table S5 |
| `lvp` (V2) | log(1.23 L) | Table S5 |
| `lq` (Q) | log(1.32 L/day) | Table S5 |
| `e_wt_cl_exp_inf`, `e_wt_vc`, `e_wt_vp` | 0.639, 0.378, 1.08 | Table S5; `(WT/75)^theta` (Table 1) |
| `e_alb_cl_exp_inf` | -0.682 | Table S5; `(ALB/40)^theta` (Table 1) |
| `e_age_cl_exp_inf` | -0.241 | Table S5; `(AGE/65)^theta` (Table 1) |
| `e_tumsz_cl_exp_inf`, `e_tumsz_cl_exp_component` | 0.09, 0.351 | Table S5; `(BSIZ/3000)^theta` (Table 1) |
| `e_sex_cl_exp_inf`, `e_sex_cl_exp_component`, `e_sex_vc` | 1.18, 1.45, 1.19 | Table S5; male vs female reference (Table 1) |
| `e_tumtp_cll_cl_exp_inf`, `e_tumtp_sll_cl_exp_inf`, `e_tumtp_mcl_cl_exp_inf` | 1.47, 1.38, 2.07 | Table S5; vs FL or DLBCL (Table 1) |
| `e_tumtp_cll_cl_exp_component`, `e_tumtp_mcl_cl_exp_component` | 2.25, 2.80 | Table S5; vs FL or DLBCL (Table 1) |
| `e_conmed_chop_cl_exp_kdes`, `e_conmed_bendamustine_cl_exp_kdes`, `e_conmed_fc_cl_exp_kdes` | 0.309, 0.591, 2.64 | Table S5; Table 1 |
| `e_tumtp_mzl_cl_exp_kdes` | 0.299 | Table S5; Table 1 |
| `sdL`, `sdH`, `sd50` | 1.77, 0.111, 8.26 ug/mL | Table S5 and its footnote |
| `etalcl_exp_kdes` ... `etalq` | 0.82, 1.21, 0.199, 0.0341, 0.23, 0.956 | Table S5 omega^2 |
| `etaRUV` | 0.224 | Table S5 omega^2 EPS, IIV on the residual SD |
| `cl <- cl_exp_component * exp(-cl_exp_kdes * time) + cl_exp_inf` | n/a | Methods, "Population PK analysis" |
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)` | n/a | Methods ("2-compartment model") |
| `w <- (sdL - (sdL - sdH) * Cc / (sd50 + Cc)) * exp(etaRUV)`; `Cc ~ lnorm(w)` | n/a | Table S5 footnote (exponential residual error; SD = (sdH + sdL)/2 at sd50) |

# Deterministic checks of the model file

## Covariate effects (Table 1)

Table 1 lists the percentage change of each parameter at the 2.5th and 97.5th
percentiles of the continuous covariates, and for each category, relative to
the reference subject (65-year-old woman with FL or DLBCL, 75 kg, albumin
40 g/L, tumour size 3000 mm^2, no partner chemotherapy). These follow from the
typical values alone.

```{r table1}
mod <- readModelDb("Gibiansky_2019_obinutuzumab")

ref <- data.frame(
  WT = 75, ALB = 40, AGE = 65, SEXF = 1, TUMSZ = 3000,
  TUMTP_CLL = 0, TUMTP_MCL = 0, TUMTP_SLL = 0, TUMTP_MZL = 0,
  CONMED_CHOP = 0, CONMED_BENDAMUSTINE = 0, CONMED_FC = 0
)
scen <- tibble::tribble(
  ~parameter, ~covariate, ~value, ~published,
  "cl_exp_inf", "WT", 52, -20.9,
  "cl_exp_inf", "WT", 115, 31.4,
  "cl_exp_inf", "ALB", 28.7, 25.4,
  "cl_exp_inf", "ALB", 48.7, -12.6,
  "cl_exp_inf", "SEXF", 0, 17.6,
  "cl_exp_inf", "TUMTP_CLL", 1, 46.9,
  "cl_exp_inf", "TUMTP_SLL", 1, 38,
  "cl_exp_inf", "TUMTP_MCL", 1, 106.9,
  "cl_exp_inf", "AGE", 38, 13.8,
  "cl_exp_inf", "AGE", 83, -5.7,
  "cl_exp_inf", "TUMSZ", 304, -18.6,
  "cl_exp_inf", "TUMSZ", 22400, 19.8,
  "cl_exp_component", "SEXF", 0, 45.1,
  "cl_exp_component", "TUMTP_CLL", 1, 125.1,
  "cl_exp_component", "TUMTP_MCL", 1, 180.3,
  "cl_exp_component", "TUMSZ", 304, -55.2,
  "cl_exp_component", "TUMSZ", 22400, 102.3,
  "vc", "WT", 52, -12.9,
  "vc", "WT", 115, 17.5,
  "vc", "SEXF", 0, 19.4,
  "vp", "WT", 52, -32.6,
  "vp", "WT", 115, 58.4,
  "cl_exp_kdes", "CONMED_CHOP", 1, -69.1,
  "cl_exp_kdes", "CONMED_FC", 1, 164.4,
  "cl_exp_kdes", "CONMED_BENDAMUSTINE", 1, -40.9,
  "cl_exp_kdes", "TUMTP_MZL", 1, -70.1
)

# One subject per scenario (id 1 is the reference subject); a single
# observation at time 0 returns the individual parameters.
cov_rows <- ref[rep(1, nrow(scen) + 1), ]
for (i in seq_len(nrow(scen))) {
  cov_rows[i + 1, scen$covariate[i]] <- scen$value[i]
}
ev_par <- cbind(id = seq_len(nrow(cov_rows)), time = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central", cov_rows)
par <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_par, omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(nrow(par) == nrow(scen) + 1)

scen$model <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(scen)), function(i) {
  100 * (par[[scen$parameter[i]]][i + 1] / par[[scen$parameter[i]]][1] - 1)
}, numeric(1))

scen |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = round(model, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Parameter" = parameter, "Covariate" = covariate, "Covariate value" = value,
    "Published change (%)" = published, "Model change (%)" = model
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Covariate effects: model versus Table 1 of Gibiansky 2019.")

# Table 1 is computed from unrounded estimates and printed to one decimal;
# Table S5 rounds the factors to 3 significant digits. The largest
# difference is 0.4 points (for example V1 in men: factor 1.19 printed,
# +19.4% in Table 1).
stopifnot(max(abs(scen$model - scen$published)) < 0.75)
```

## Half-life of the time-dependent clearance

The Results give the half-life of the `CL_T` decay, `log(2) / k_des`, for the
reference subject (6.3 days) and for several disease and treatment groups.

```{r kdes-half-lives}
ref_par <- par[1, ]
kdes_ref <- ref_par$cl_exp_kdes
theta <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta
half_lives <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~factor, ~published,
  "Reference (FL or DLBCL, no partner chemotherapy)", 1, 6.3,
  "Marginal zone lymphoma", theta[["e_tumtp_mzl_cl_exp_kdes"]], 21.1,
  "CLL treated with chlorambucil (Results) = CHOP factor (Table S5)", theta[["e_conmed_chop_cl_exp_kdes"]], 20.4,
  "iNHL treated with bendamustine", theta[["e_conmed_bendamustine_cl_exp_kdes"]], 10.7,
  "FL treated with fludarabine + cyclophosphamide", theta[["e_conmed_fc_cl_exp_kdes"]], 2.4
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = log(2) / (kdes_ref * factor))

half_lives |>
  dplyr::transmute(group, published, model = round(model, 2)) |>
  dplyr::rename("Group" = group, "Published half-life (day)" = published, "Model half-life (day)" = model) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Half-life of the time-dependent clearance, model versus Results.")

stopifnot(max(abs(half_lives$model - half_lives$published)) < 0.1)
```

All five values agree. The fourth row needs a comment. The Results attribute
the 20.4-day half-life to "CLL treated with chlorambucil", but Tables 1 and
S5 list no chlorambucil or CLL effect on `k_des`. The 20.4 days is exactly
the CHOP factor (0.309) applied to the reference `k_des`. The library model
follows the tables: `CONMED_CHOP` carries the 0.309 factor, and a CLL patient
on chlorambucil gets the reference `k_des` (half-life 6.3 days). See
Assumptions and deviations.

## Residual error

The Table S5 footnote defines `sigma_50` as the concentration at which the SD
of the exponential residual error is `(sigma_H + sigma_L) / 2`. The hyperbolic
form in the model meets that definition:

```{r residual-check}
w_at <- function(conc) {
  theta[["sdL"]] - (theta[["sdL"]] - theta[["sdH"]]) * conc / (theta[["sd50"]] + conc)
}
stopifnot(abs(w_at(theta[["sd50"]]) - (theta[["sdL"]] + theta[["sdH"]]) / 2) < 1e-12)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  `Concentration (ug/mL)` = c(1, 8.26, 100, 400),
  `Log-scale residual SD` = round(w_at(c(1, 8.26, 100, 400)), 3),
  check.names = FALSE
), caption = "Typical residual SD (before the etaRUV random effect) at selected concentrations.")
```

# Replicate Figure S3: typical-value predictions in FL

Supplementary Figure S3 shows "predictive simulations" of the iNHL regimen
in follicular lymphoma: 1000 mg on days 0, 7, 14, 28, 56, 84, 112 and 140,
then on days 200, 260, 320 and 380 (Supplementary Methods). Panel A compares
women and men, panel B disease types under obinutuzumab monotherapy, and
panel C the partner chemotherapies. The curves turn out to be typical-value
profiles at the Table 1 reference covariates: the female monotherapy curve
of panel A passes within a few percent of the reference subject at every
trough. The maintainers digitised the curves from the supplement images by
pixel colour, at 0.5-1 day before each dose and at day 300.

```{r figure-s3-sim}
dose_times <- c(0, 7, 14, 28, 56, 84, 112, 140, 200, 260, 320, 380)
# Infusion duration is not reported; 4 h is used for every infusion.
inf_dur <- 4 / 24

s3_scen <- list(
  "Women (reference)" = list(),
  "Men" = list(SEXF = 0),
  "MCL" = list(TUMTP_MCL = 1),
  "SLL" = list(TUMTP_SLL = 1),
  "MZL" = list(TUMTP_MZL = 1),
  "CLL" = list(TUMTP_CLL = 1),
  "With CHOP" = list(CONMED_CHOP = 1),
  "With FC" = list(CONMED_FC = 1),
  "With bendamustine" = list(CONMED_BENDAMUSTINE = 1)
)
obs_s3 <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 301, by = 0.25), 6.5, 27.5, 55.5, 83.5, 111.5, 139.5, 199, 259)))
ev_s3 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(s3_scen), function(i) {
  cv <- ref
  for (k in names(s3_scen[[i]])) cv[[k]] <- s3_scen[[i]][[k]]
  doses <- data.frame(time = dose_times[dose_times <= 300], evid = 1L, amt = 1000, cmt = "central")
  doses$rate <- doses$amt / inf_dur
  obs <- data.frame(time = obs_s3, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", rate = 0)
  ev <- rbind(doses, obs)
  cbind(id = i, scenario = names(s3_scen)[i], ev, cv[rep(1, nrow(ev)), ])
})) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev_s3, keep = "scenario", returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(all(typ$Cc >= 0))

panel <- c(
  "Women (reference)" = "A: sex", "Men" = "A: sex",
  "MCL" = "B: disease type", "SLL" = "B: disease type", "MZL" = "B: disease type", "CLL" = "B: disease type",
  "With CHOP" = "C: partner chemotherapy", "With FC" = "C: partner chemotherapy",
  "With bendamustine" = "C: partner chemotherapy"
)
typ |>
  dplyr::mutate(panel = panel[scenario]) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    typ |>
      dplyr::filter(scenario == "Women (reference)") |>
      dplyr::mutate(scenario = "FL monotherapy (reference)", panel = "B: disease type"),
    typ |>
      dplyr::filter(scenario == "Women (reference)") |>
      dplyr::mutate(scenario = "Monotherapy (reference)", panel = "C: partner chemotherapy")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 7, Cc, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Concentration (ug/mL)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure S3 A-C of Gibiansky 2019 (typical-value profiles)."
  )
```

```{r figure-s3-compare}
digitised <- tibble::tribble(

  "MCL", 27.5, 247, "MCL", 55.5, 165, "MCL", 83.5, 149, "MCL", 111.5, 141,
  "MCL", 139.5, 128, "MCL", 300, 63,
  "SLL", 27.5, 385, "SLL", 55.5, 298, "SLL", 83.5, 273, "SLL", 111.5, 256,
  "SLL", 139.5, 244, "SLL", 199, 104, "SLL", 300, 116,
  "MZL", 27.5, 336, "MZL", 55.5, 257, "MZL", 111.5, 298, "MZL", 139.5, 321,
  "MZL", 199, 182,
  "With CHOP", 27.5, 339, "With CHOP", 55.5, 266, "With CHOP", 83.5, 283,
  "With CHOP", 111.5, 305, "With CHOP", 139.5, 326,

)
s3_cmp <- digitised |>
  dplyr::inner_join(typ[, c("scenario", "time", "Cc")], by = c("scenario", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (Cc / published - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(s3_cmp) == nrow(digitised))

s3_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = round(Cc), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Scenario" = scenario, "Day" = time, "Figure S3 (ug/mL)" = published,
    "Model (ug/mL)" = Cc, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value troughs: model versus digitised Figure S3.")

# The comparison is deterministic (typical values, no random effects); the
# residual differences are digitisation error, largest at the steep day-6.5
# points. A wrong factor, exponent or reference value moves a whole scenario
# by tens of percent.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(s3_cmp$pct_diff)) < 3,
  quantile(abs(s3_cmp$pct_diff), 0.9) < 6
)
```

Every scenario, including the slower decay of `CL_T` with CHOP and MZL
(troughs rising over cycles 2-6) and the faster decay with FC, reproduces the
supplement figure. The digitised CLL curve is dashed and overlaps the others,
so it is plotted but not tabulated.

# Virtual GADOLIN cohort

The exposure-response analyses used follicular lymphoma patients treated
with obinutuzumab plus bendamustine in GADOLIN. The cohort below has 200
virtual FL patients on bendamustine with covariates drawn to match the
GADOLIN column of Table S4: age 61.7 (SD 11.2) years, weight 80.8 (17.2) kg,
albumin 39.9 (4.8) g/L and tumour size 4500 (4460) mm^2 (log-normal). The
paper does not report sex; half the cohort is female. The random effects
come from R's random number generator (a Latin hypercube over the
standard-normal marginals, scaled by the Table S5 variances) and the solve
uses `omega = NA`, so the cohort is identical on any machine or solver
thread count.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20190501)
n <- 200
lognormal <- function(n, m, s, lo, hi) {
  sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (s / m)^2))
  pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(m) - sdlog^2 / 2, sdlog)), lo), hi)
}
subjects <- data.frame(
  sid = seq_len(n),
  SEXF = sample(rep(0:1, length.out = n)),
  WT = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 80.8, 17.2), 45), 150),
  ALB = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 39.9, 4.8), 25), 52),
  AGE = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 61.7, 11.2), 25), 90),
  TUMSZ = lognormal(n, 4500, 4460, 100, 40000),
  TUMTP_CLL = 0, TUMTP_MCL = 0, TUMTP_SLL = 0, TUMTP_MZL = 0,
  CONMED_CHOP = 0, CONMED_BENDAMUSTINE = 1, CONMED_FC = 0
)

omega <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$omega
z <- vapply(seq_len(ncol(omega)), function(j) qnorm((sample.int(n) - 0.5) / n), numeric(n))
etas <- z %*% chol(omega)
colnames(etas) <- colnames(omega)
subjects <- cbind(subjects, etas)

subjects |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(c(AGE, WT, ALB, TUMSZ), ~ sprintf("%.3g (%.3g)", mean(.x), sd(.x)))) |>
  dplyr::mutate(`Female (%)` = 100 * mean(subjects$SEXF)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Virtual cohort, mean (SD). Table S4 GADOLIN: age 61.7 (11.2) years, weight 80.8 (17.2) kg, albumin 39.9 (4.8) g/L, tumour size 4500 (4460) mm^2.")
```

```{r events}
# Dense sampling through induction (for the induction-period Cmean) and a
# 180-day washout after the last maintenance dose (for the terminal
# half-life).
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(0, 168, by = 0.5), seq(170, 380, by = 2), seq(382, 560, by = 2),
  dose_times + inf_dur
)))
events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
  s <- subjects[i, ]
  doses <- data.frame(time = dose_times, evid = 1L, amt = 1000, cmt = "central", rate = 1000 / inf_dur)
  obs <- data.frame(time = obs_times, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", rate = 0)
  ev <- rbind(doses, obs)
  cbind(id = i, treatment = "G-Benda", ev, s[rep(1, nrow(ev)), names(s) != "sid"])
})) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, omega = NA, keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(all(sim$Cc >= 0))

# The supplied random effects are applied: the realised between-subject SD
# of log(CL_T), after removing the covariate effects, equals sqrt(omega^2).
first_row <- sim[!duplicated(sim$id), ]
stopifnot(abs(sd(first_row$etalcl_exp_component) - sqrt(1.21)) < 0.05)

pct <- sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(pct, aes(time / 7)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q50), colour = "red") +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q05), colour = "navy") +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q95), colour = "navy") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Concentration (ug/mL)",
    caption = "Virtual GADOLIN FL cohort on bendamustine: median (red), 5th and 95th percentiles (blue); compare Figure S2."
  )
```

Figure S2 of the paper is a conditional simulation with the individual
parameters of the analysis patients, so only its general shape (steady
state reached by the end of cycle 1, medians of roughly 300-600 ug/mL
through induction) is comparable with a population simulation.

# Exposure over the induction period (PKNCA)

The exposure-response analyses use `Cmean`, the cumulative AUC from the first
dose to 28 days after the last induction dose divided by that duration
(Supplementary Methods); with the nominal regimen this is `AUC(0-168 d) / 168`,
which PKNCA computes as `cav`. Table 2 gives the `Cmean` tertile boundaries
in the 128 G-Benda patients of the PFS analysis (141, 313, 400 and
794 ug/mL), and the Results give its 5th and 95th percentiles (195 and
604 ug/mL).

```{r pknca-induction}
conc_ind <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), time <= 168) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
dose_all <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, amt)
stopifnot(all(tapply(conc_ind$time, conc_ind$id, min) == 0))

nca_ind <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_ind, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_all, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 168, cav = TRUE, cmax = TRUE)
))
cmean <- as.data.frame(nca_ind$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "cav")
stopifnot(nrow(cmean) == n, !anyNA(cmean$PPORRES))

q_cmp <- data.frame(
  quantile = c("5th", "33.3rd (lower tertile boundary)", "66.7th (upper tertile boundary)", "95th"),
  published = c(195, 313, 400, 604),
  simulated = unname(quantile(cmean$PPORRES, c(0.05, 1 / 3, 2 / 3, 0.95)))
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated / published - 1))
q_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(simulated = round(simulated), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Percentile" = quantile, "Published Cmean (ug/mL)" = published,
    "Simulated Cmean (ug/mL)" = simulated, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Induction-period Cmean distribution: virtual cohort versus Table 2 and Results.")

# Tertile boundaries are robust quantiles of the cohort; the patients' own
# dosing delays and reductions are not simulated, so a modest excess is
# expected. A clearance or dose error moves both boundaries by tens of percent.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(q_cmp$pct_diff[2:3])) < 15,
  max(abs(q_cmp$pct_diff[2:3])) < 20
)
```

The tertile boundaries agree within 7%. The simulated tails are wider than
the published 5th and 95th percentiles (the 5th percentile most of all). The
published `Cmean` values come from post hoc individual parameters, which are
shrunk towards the typical values (Table S5 shrinkage 27% for `CL_T` and 26%
for `k_des`), while the virtual cohort draws the full between-subject
variability; patients who stopped before five doses were also excluded from
the published set. The tails are therefore shown but not gated.

# Individual PK parameters and terminal half-life (Table S6)

Table S6 summarises the individual (post hoc) PK parameters of the 406 FL
patients: median `CL_inf` 0.0821 L/day, `V1` 2.96 L, `Vss` 4.32 L and
terminal half-life 37.5 days, the last computed after `CL_T` has decayed to
zero. The virtual cohort gives the same quantities from its individual
parameters, and PKNCA gives the terminal half-life from the 180-day washout
after the last maintenance dose, by which time `CL_T` has vanished.

```{r table-s6}
ind <- first_row |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    k10 = cl_exp_inf / vc, k12 = q / vc, k21 = q / vp,
    a = k10 + k12 + k21,
    beta = 0.5 * (a - sqrt(a^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)),
    thalf = log(2) / beta,
    vss = vc + vp
  )
s6 <- data.frame(
  parameter = c("CL_inf (L/day)", "V1 (L)", "Vss (L)", "Terminal half-life (day)"),
  published = c(0.0821, 2.96, 4.32, 37.5),
  simulated = c(median(ind$cl_exp_inf), median(ind$vc), median(ind$vss), median(ind$thalf))
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated / published - 1))
s6 |>
  dplyr::mutate(simulated = signif(simulated, 3), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Parameter" = parameter, "Table S6 FL median" = published,
    "Virtual cohort median" = simulated, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median individual PK parameters: virtual FL cohort versus Table S6.")
stopifnot(max(abs(s6$pct_diff)) < 15)
```

```{r pknca-terminal}
conc_term <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), time >= 380) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = time - 380) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
dose_term <- dose_all |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 380) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0)
stopifnot(all(tapply(conc_term$time, conc_term$id, min) == 0))
nca_term <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_term, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_term, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))

reference_s6 <- data.frame(treatment = "G-Benda", PPTESTCD = "half.life", PPORRES = 37.5)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_term,
  reference = reference_s6,
  by = "treatment",
  params = "half.life",
  units = c(half.life = "day"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Terminal half-life after the last maintenance dose (PKNCA, cohort median) versus the Table S6 FL median. * differs by more than 20%.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Covariate functional forms.** The paper prints the estimates (Table S5)
  and the effect sizes (Table 1) but not the model code. Continuous
  covariates enter as power functions of the covariate over the Table 1
  reference (median) value and categorical covariates as multiplicative
  factors; this reproduces all 26 rows of Table 1 to within 0.4 percentage
  points (the rounding of Table S5).
* **Chlorambucil and `k_des`.** The Results quote a 20.4-day `CL_T` half-life
  for "CLL treated with chlorambucil", which equals the CHOP factor of Table
  S5 (0.309) on the reference `k_des`. Neither table lists a chlorambucil or
  CLL effect on `k_des`. The library model follows the tables (the CHOP
  factor applies to CHOP only), so a CLL patient on chlorambucil gets the
  reference half-life of 6.3 days. If the analysis pooled chlorambucil with
  CHOP into one indicator, setting `CONMED_CHOP = 1` for CLL11-type
  chlorambucil patients would reproduce the 20.4 days quoted in the Results.
* **Reference sex.** The reference subject is female (Results; Table 1), so
  the male factors are applied as `theta^(1 - SEXF)`.
* **Missing covariates.** The paper does not state how missing albumin or
  tumour size were handled; supply a value for every subject (for example the
  reference value).
* **Time origin.** `CL_T` decays with time since the first obinutuzumab dose;
  simulations must start at the first dose.
* **Residual error.** The exponential residual error is encoded as a
  log-scale SD falling from `sdL` to `sdH` with concentration, times
  `exp(etaRUV)`, the form defined by the Table S5 footnote and used in the
  authors' later rituximab model (Gibiansky 2021). The paper does not print
  the equation itself.
* **IIV.** Table S5 reports variances only; the random effects are
  independent.
* **Infusion duration.** Not reported; 4 hours for every infusion.
* **Virtual cohort.** Covariates were drawn independently from the GADOLIN
  column of Table S4, with half the cohort female (sex is not reported). The
  nominal regimen of the Supplementary Methods simulations is used, without
  the dosing delays and modifications that entered the patients' `Cmean`.
* **Figure S3 digitisation.** Values were read from the supplement images by
  pixel colour at 0.5-1 day before each dose and at day 300, calibrated on
  the axis ticks.
* **Errata.** No correction notice was found for this article as of
  2026-11-25 (Crossref).
